article.dek: Friday's final injury designations are in, Cleveland has a new starting quarterback, and the Giants moved across the key number of 3 — here is what changed since this morning.

items.headline: Lead: Friday's designations are in — and Cleveland has a new starting quarterback
paragraphs: The last real information before Sunday landed this afternoon. Every team has now filed its final injury designations for Week 9, and the headline is at quarterback: Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland on Sunday at New Orleans. Head coach Todd Monken announced it Friday. Deshaun Watson stays in the concussion protocol and is listed as questionable.

Sanders took the first-team reps all week. It is his first start of the season. He started seven games last year and went 3-4. The Saints are 3-point favorites at home, and just 13% of the money at DraftKings has come in on Cleveland so far.

The other quarterback calls did not move. Seattle's Sam Darnold is officially out against Arizona with quad and rib injuries — he did not practice all week. Drew Lock starts, and he has been limited all week with a right elbow injury. In Philadelphia, Joe Milton still starts against the Giants with Jalen Hurts out for the season.
One more quarterback note: Arizona traded backup Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore on Friday. That is the team that just started rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday night.
items.takeaway: Sanders starts for Cleveland with Watson in the concussion protocol; Darnold is out and Lock starts for Seattle; Milton still starts for Philadelphia.

items.headline: The designation rundown: who is out, who is questionable
paragraphs: Atlanta loses two starters for the Madrid game against Cincinnati: wide receiver Zachariah Branch and running back Brian Robinson Jr. are both out with hamstring injuries. Robinson misses his third straight game. Cincinnati ruled out safety Kyle Dugger with a quad injury.

New England ruled out wide receiver A.J. Brown for a second straight game with ankle and knee injuries, and running back TreVeyon Henderson is out with an illness. Tight end Hunter Henry is questionable with a foot injury. Green Bay's tight end Josh Whyle is out with a concussion.

The Jets will not have their top weapon at Kansas City: wide receiver Garrett Wilson is out with a concussion. Kansas City ruled out defensive tackles Peter Woods and Omarr Norman-Lott and cornerback Mansoor Delane, but wide receiver Rashee Rice and tight end Travis Kelce practiced fully and carry no designation.

Arizona ruled out right guard Jon Gaines II, running back Bam Knight and left tackle Jayden Williams for the trip to Seattle. Houston ruled out running back David Montgomery with a groin injury and safety Reed Blankenship with a concussion. The Chargers ruled out cornerback Deane Leonard and safety Kendall Williamson, and wide receiver Brenen Thompson is doubtful. Miami listed three players as questionable against Detroit, and Chicago listed running back Kyle Monangai as questionable for Sunday night.
That is the full picture now. The next update is the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday.
items.takeaway: Garrett Wilson, A.J. Brown, Brian Robinson Jr. and David Montgomery are among the players ruled out; Hunter Henry and Kyle Monangai are questionable.

items.headline: Weather: still calm — Seattle and New England have the only wind worth noting
paragraphs: The final forecast for Sunday did not change the morning read. No outdoor game carries a real weather problem. The National Weather Service data, pulled Friday afternoon, flags zero games for wind.

The two windiest spots are the same two as this morning. Arizona at Seattle, 4:25 p.m. ET at Lumen Field, has wind around 12 to 13 miles per hour with gusts to about 25, around 55 degrees, with a chance of light drizzle. Green Bay at New England, also 4:25 p.m. ET, is similar — wind near 12 miles per hour gusting to 25 or 26, around 53 degrees, clear.

Everywhere else is quiet. The Jets at Kansas City is near 60 degrees and clear with a light wind. Detroit at Miami is the warmest game of the week, in the low 80s. The Bengals and Falcons play in Madrid at 9:30 a.m. ET under a retractable roof. Dallas at Indianapolis is under a retractable roof too, and Cleveland at New Orleans and Houston at the Chargers are indoors.
That is a factual weather read, not a totals edge. Wind is the weather that matters most for football, and nothing on this slate is strong enough to build a bet around on its own.
items.takeaway: Sunday is calm: the windiest games are Seattle and New England with gusts to about 25, and nothing else is close to a weather problem.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Read again after the evening refresh, at about 6:10 p.m. Denver time, the app board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. It has not flipped, and it has not picked up any of the Sunday quarterback changes.

The quarterback fields are stale across the board. Baltimore's quarterback field is blank — it never picked up Fagnano as Thursday's starter. Cleveland still lists Deshaun Watson, but Shedeur Sanders starts on Sunday. Seattle still lists Sam Darnold, but he is out and Drew Lock starts. If you read a Sunday quarterback off this board, you are reading last week.

So there is still no Sunday card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. If your book has a Sunday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

The only cards on the board are Monday's Chicago at Seattle game, which has already been played. They are worth one look because they show how the three cards differ, and the numbers are unchanged from this morning. The Value card and the Balanced card were the same play: Chicago +3 at -102, with the model giving Chicago a 50.6% chance against a market price implying 46.5% — a +3.6% edge. The Hit Rate card was Seattle on the moneyline at -175, with the model at 56.1% against a market price implying 60.4%. Hit Rate is the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. It is not the best value. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Sunday's prices go through Check until the board flips.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets — two numbers that tell different stories
paragraphs: When you see betting splits, you will usually see two percentages side by side: handle and tickets. Tickets, sometimes labeled BET, is the share of the number of bets. Handle, labeled HND, is the share of the money. They can point in different directions, and that is the whole point of reading them.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40% of the handle is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and a smaller number of bigger bets on the underdog. The crowd is on one side and the money is on the other.

Why it matters: a split like that is a question, not an answer. It tells you the two sides of the market disagree, and the next thing to watch is the price. If the line moves toward the side with the handle, the money may be winning the argument. If it does not move at all, the books may be happy to keep taking the ticket side. Either way, one book's split on its own is never enough — you want a second book or a real line move before it means anything.
items.takeaway: Tickets count the bets, handle counts the money — when they disagree, watch the price next, and never trust one book's split on its own.

items.headline: Friday's moves: the Giants crossed 3, the Chiefs total kept climbing
paragraphs: The Giants moved across a key number today. DraftKings is now dealing the Giants at -3.5 against Philadelphia, up from -3 this morning and -2.5 at the open. The total in that game fell from 40.5 at the open to 38.5. A half-point across 3 is worth more than a half-point anywhere else, so if your book still has the Giants at -3, that is the better side of the same bet.

The Chiefs-Jets total kept climbing. DraftKings opened it at 43.5 and it is now 47.5, up four points, with the Chiefs now -10 after sitting at -9.5 this morning. The Lions-Dolphins total ticked up a point too, from 49.5 to 50.5. Dallas went back to -5.5 at Indianapolis after sitting at -5 this morning, and the total there dropped a point to 51.5. Houston ticked up to -6 at the Chargers, and the Rams came down to -4.5 at Washington after opening at -5.5.

The app has not caught any of this yet. The board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, so none of these prices are on a card. If your book has a line you like, run it through Check: type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The Giants moved to -3.5 across the key number of 3, the Chiefs total climbed four points to 47.5, and Dallas went back to -5.5.

items.headline: The designations are in — bet the good number now
paragraphs: This morning's tip said to wait for Friday's final designations. They are in now, and that was the last real information event before Sunday. Inactives do not come until about 90 minutes before kickoff, and by then the good numbers are usually gone.

So do not keep waiting. If your book has a Sunday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number Sunday, because the Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push the line the wrong way. A quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be.
items.takeaway: The designations are in, so run your book's Sunday price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now.
